- When sentiment is negative and forecast shows a sharp upward move, reduce the forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent history shows a strong downward trend and forecast is still falling, check for lag — adjust downward bias by 2–3% per negative sentiment day.  
- After a spike in price (e.g., >10% above recent mean), forecast should not overshoot — cap upward revisions at +5% of prior peak.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model should not forecast a sustained upward trend — apply mean reversion bias toward 10–15% below recent high.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is >10% above forecast, check if sentiment was positive — if so, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence.  
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive but forecast is consistently below true outcome, add 1–3% upward bias to avoid underestimating momentum.
